body: ## Problem The README currently has no screenshot. Users have to run the dashboard locally to see what it looks like. ## Solution Add a screenshot to the README showing the real app rendered with the deterministic simulated dataset (`?simulate=1`). ## Implementation 1. **Start the dashboard with simulation mode**: ```bash uv run python app.py ``` 2. **Capture screenshot via Playwright** (already configured in `scripts/snapshot_dashboard.py`): ```bash uv run --with playwright python scripts/snapshot_dashboard.py --url "http://localhost:8321/?simulate=1" ``` This outputs to `dashboard-snapshots/` with a timestamped PNG and a DOM summary JSON. 3. **Add the screenshot to the repo** (e.g., `docs/dashboard-screenshot.png`) and reference it in the README: ```markdown ## Screenshot *Simulated dataset — deterministic mock data for consistent screenshots and regression checks.* ``` 4. **Update README** to mention the screenshot near the top (after the one-liner description) and add a note that `?simulate=1` produces deterministic mock data. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Screenshot captured from real app with `?simulate=1` - [ ] Screenshot added to repo (committed) - [ ] README updated with screenshot and caption - [ ] Screenshot width is reasonable for GitHub rendering (800-1000px) - [ ] Dashboard visual includes: Overview cards, Tool Sources, Daily chart, Model Breakdown table, Usage History ## Notes - The simulation mode (`?simulate=1` or `DASHBOARD_SIMULATE=1`) is already implemented and deterministic — designed for this exact purpose - The snapshot script already handles authentication, waits for chart render, and produces both PNG + DOM summary - No code changes needed beyond the README edit and adding the image asset
title: Improve README with real app screenshot (mocked data via simulate=1)
